title: GECDSB trustees to review $1M cut to textbooks and classroom supplies
executiveSummary: The Greater Essex County District School Board is facing a $1 million funding cut because 120 fewer students enrolled than expected.
To offset the loss, board staff plan to save $1 million by reducing discretionary spending on textbooks and classroom supplies.
Trustees will also review millions of dollars in recently awarded school renovation contracts and a new student safety aide program.
studentParentImpact: Because GECDSB enrolment is down by 120 students, the board is losing $1 million in provincial funding. To keep the projected year-end deficit at $3.6 million, the board is cutting $1 million from textbooks and classroom supplies. This means schools will have less money for discretionary learning materials this year. On the positive side, families will see upgrades at several local schools. Trustees will review completed contracts for a new field house at Riverside Secondary, daycare renovations at Dougall Public School, and accessibility upgrades at Belle River, Northwood, Ford City, and Southwood schools. The agenda does not list a way for the public to participate in this meeting.
policyChanges: The board will review its annual report on Policy BA-02 (Borrowing and Investing of Funds), which shows no new investments or energy price hedging agreements were made last year.

title: GECDSB trustees to review student math, mental health, and Indigenous plans
executiveSummary: Greater Essex County District School Board trustees will review end-of-year math results and plans for digital math tools.
Staff will present updates on student mental health services, including over 1,100 social work referrals last year.
The board will outline the 2026-2027 Indigenous Action Plan, which includes free tutoring and support workers.
studentParentImpact: At this meeting, Greater Essex County District School Board trustees will hear updates on key student programs across Windsor and surrounding areas. For math, elementary and secondary students will see continued small-group instruction and new digital tools like KnowledgeHook next school year. Indigenous students can access 20 to 26 hours of free tutoring per semester in math and English, alongside support from graduation coaches and student support workers. Families can also expect continued mental health initiatives, including social work support and classroom wellness modules. The agenda does not list a way for the public to speak or submit comments at this meeting.
policyChanges: No board policy or procedure is up for creation, revision, or rescinding on this agenda.

title: GECDSB to vote on new rules for naming and renaming local schools
executiveSummary: GECDSB trustees will vote on a new policy requiring provincial approval before naming or renaming any local school.
The board plans to review all school names every five years to ensure they do not represent a legacy of harm.
Other updates would restrict trustee expenses and change how community partnerships and budget controls are managed.
studentParentImpact: Under the proposed school naming policy, GECDSB families will have a direct say when schools are built, consolidated, or renamed. The board will set up Naming Advisory Committees that must include parents, students, and community representatives. Before choosing a name, the board will run public surveys and student focus groups to gather feedback. Additionally, school names across Windsor and Essex County will be reviewed every five years to ensure they align with diversity and equity values. Parents can apply to serve on these naming committees when a local school project is approved.
policyChanges: The board is voting to approve new or revised policies on School Naming, Trustee Expenses, Board Member Honoraria, Budget Control, and Community Partnerships. It also plans to rescind policies on Environmental Education, Video Surveillance, and External Student Research, converting them into operational procedures.
